key_insight: A turbulence-aware 3D reconstruction framework combines multiscale neural operators, temporal state-space modeling, and physics-based residual constraints to recover high-fidelity flow fields from coarse data.
engineering_relevance: This enables cheaper, more accurate surrogate reconstruction of turbulent volumes for CFD analysis, monitoring, and downstream scientific or engineering decision-making.
method: Multiscale neural operator reconstructs volumetric fine-scale spatial structures from coarse-grained inputs.
State-space model enforces coherent time evolution across reconstructed flow snapshots.
Navier–Stokes residuals and a mixture-of-experts module add physical regularization and adaptivity to unknown coarse-graining.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved reconstruction error and better preservation of multiscale spatial structure and temporal coherence on canonical turbulent systems and atmospheric reanalysis data.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the model generalizes across different coarse-graining patterns and turbulence regimes, especially where physics residuals are only soft constraints.
paper_title: High-fidelity Three-Dimensional Flow Field Reconstruction Driven by Turbulent Fluid Dynamics
